fatal_errors: The proposed as-cast polycrystalline specimens introduce grain-size, texture, segregation, and casting-defect effects absent from the homogenized single-crystal comparison, preventing clean attribution to local lattice distortion.
Composition is used to vary lattice distortion without controlling correlated changes in modulus, stacking-fault energy, chemical interactions, magnetism, and short-range order.

XRD peak broadening is not a composition-specific measure of static local lattice distortion unless contributions from crystallite size, dislocations, residual stress, and instrumental broadening are separated.
The claimed transition from large mismatch to localized stress and brittle failure is unsupported by cited evidence and was not established by the target study.
explanation: The hypothesis recovers one important part of the target: composition-dependent local lattice distortion can increase solid-solution glide resistance, and a controlled compositional series could test whether strength scales with an independently measured distortion metric. It does not reconstruct the central temperature-resolved experiment or its distinct regimes: thermally activated glide and phonon-drag-related inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, or Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type dynamic solute pinning and serrated Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening at high temperature. The room-temperature, generic polycrystal design also differs substantially from the [1̄23]-oriented FCC single-crystal CRSS comparison and cannot isolate intrinsic slip resistance. Its falsification rule is directionally useful but weakly discriminating because composition simultaneously changes many variables. No prior evidence is cited, and the ductility/brittle-failure extension is speculative. Thus it is a partial reconstruction of the MSAD/lattice-distortion strengthening component, not a reconstruction of the complete governing mechanism.
